action_summary: Round 7 read what a program declares when asked for help. Round 8 read what it declares when it REFUSES, and found the precondition is not knowledge to fetch or a parameter to train: it is a sentence naming the missing term. Six clause forms are read from the program's own words -- an offered flag, an enumerated mode set, a witness noun, an unloadable kind, a range, a conflict -- plus WORLD: 'fatal: not a git repository' is answered by git's own admitted `init`, which took git from 3 doors in 480 refusals to 438. Placement is part of the repair (a flag goes in the option region, a value with the operands) and a witness is accepted only when its CONTENT is the kind named.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: Four routes were measured and rejected in this round rather than argued. (1) Fetch preconditions from the web: nothing fetched from the web has moved a door in two rounds; the sentence is local. (2) A learned repair policy (PALADIN / ToolMono class): trains a model to imitate reading, and open baselines repair at most 9.6% in one shot; the refusal can be parsed instead. (3) A per-program repair table: a table of programs, the defect the census exists to avoid. (4) Appending the repaired flag at the end of the argv: measured, `openssl cms -stream in.txt -encrypt` never sees the flag because openssl stops reading options at the first operand -- the same defect round 7 found in the binder.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: OSWorld 2.0's authors diagnose frontier failure as weak recovery and maintenance of hidden state. A computer-use agent's action is only as good as the invocation it can compose from what the environment declares. Round 7 measured that the composition was wrong for reasons the environment had already published: the same 20 programs yield 33 doors when their declarations are misread and 57 when they are read, with no new knowledge acquired. No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.
